item.title: The 'life and death' decision for North Sea energy awaiting the PM
item.description: The oil and gas industry has urged Andy Burnham to approve two controversial North Sea developments as a public consultation on the UK's largest undeveloped oil field closes.
item.media:description: North Sea oil exploration platforms lie in the Cromerty Firth in northern Scotland in 2003. Pic: AP

item.title: Banking veteran Hoffman to step down as Monzo chairman
item.description: The banking industry veteran who helped steer Northern Rock back towards private sector ownership after its government rescue is handing over the reins at Monzo, the neobank which now ranks among Britain's most valuable lenders.

item.title: Eurostar rival finally gets go ahead - could it mean cheaper tickets?
item.media:description: Computer-generated image of a Virgin train at St Pancras International station. Pic: PA

item.title: Rail freight giant DB Cargo shunts UK operation into sale process
item.description: One of Britain's biggest rail freight operators is being put up for sale as its state-owned German parent confronts financial challenges in its domestic and wider European businesses.
item.media:description: A DB Cargo locomotive pulling a goods train near Burton upon Trent. Pic: iStock and Chris Hepburn

item.title: Defence investor GALLOS raises £35m amid boom for security start-ups
item.description: A defence investor which counts Sir Jeremy Fleming, the former director of GCHQ, among its advisers will this week unveil a £35m fundraising, underlining the surging appetite to fund the next wave of security and resilience start-ups.
item.media:description: StirlingX's drone supported by GALLOS Technologies, a venture builder which backs technologically advanced security start-ups. Pic: GALLOS

item.title: 'I'm a builder - here are three questions to always ask us and the upgrades that rarely help your house price'
item.description: If you've ever spent your morning commute daydreaming about starting afresh with your career, this feature is for you. Each Monday, the Money blog chats to someone from a different profession to discover what it's really like. Today we speak to builder Luke Burford, co-founder of comparebuilders.co.uk.

item.title: Au Vodka founders to toast £500m windfall from Sazerac sale
item.description: The alcoholic beverages empire co-founded by Britain's best-known former football ballboy is in advanced talks about a possible £500m sale to Sazerac Company, the American drinks giant.
item.media:description: Two women drink Au Vodka cans. Pic: Reuters

item.title: Football watchdog consults on backstop costs amid fears of New Deal stalemate
item.description: English football’s regulator is consulting on rules that will further intensify the cost pressure on clubs if the Premier League and English Football League (EFL) fail to reach agreement on a landmark financial redistribution deal.
item.media:description: Wolves and Blackburn Rovers playing the opening Championship match on Friday evening. Pic: Reuters

item.title: Harvey Nichols moves to reassure luxury brands after Frasers swoop
item.description: Bosses at Harvey Nichols are trying to reassure the department store chain's hundreds of luxury brand partners about its future stewardship under the retail tycoon Mike Ashley.
item.media:description: Harvey Nichols department store in Knightsbridge, London. PRESS ASSOCIATION Photo. Wednesday August 14, 2013. Nick Ansell/PA Wire.

item.title: UK growth slows but economy resilient despite Iran war
item.description: The rate of UK growth has slowed but the economy remained resilient despite the Iran war, according to the latest data.
